EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by two very strong C–H stretching bands at 2879 cm⁻¹ and 2906 cm⁻¹, typical of saturated aliphatic CH₂ / CH₃ groups (rule GFQ-003). Medium bands at 1442 cm⁻¹ (CH₂ scissoring) and 1306 cm⁻¹ (CH₃/CH₂ twisting–wagging) further point to a saturated, non-aromatic hydrocarbon chain. A band near 1078 cm⁻¹ matches the C–O stretch of an aliphatic alcohol, and the 894 cm⁻¹ feature is consistent with C–C–O skeletal motions seen in such alcohols. The weak 2728 cm⁻¹ band can be interpreted as an overtone/combination band often observed in long-chain alcohols. Among the candidates, structures 1, 2 and 7 are simple aliphatic alcohols; all others contain carbonyls, nitriles or nitro/azo groups that would introduce strong Raman bands (e.g., C=O ~1700 cm⁻¹, C≡N ~2250 cm⁻¹) absent from the experimental data. Candidate 1 (CCCC(O)CCC), a straight-chain secondary alcohol (4-heptanol), best fits the unbranched-chain character suggested by the spectrum, whereas candidates 2 and 7 are more highly branched, which would typically give additional CH₃ modes near 1365/1450 cm⁻¹ and 2925/2960 cm⁻¹ that are not observed. Therefore candidate 1 is the most compatible with the experimental Raman peaks.
